The interior point K is connected with several division points on the sides, dividing the large quadrilateral into 4 small quadrilaterals. The upper-left small quadrilateral is marked with area 8, the upper-right small quadrilateral is marked with area 10, the lower-left small quadrilateral is marked with area 18, and the lower-right gray small quadrilateral is marked with a question mark. The points P,Q; R,S; T,U; V,W on the sides respectively trisect the four sides of the large quadrilateral. According to the method, denote the four vertices of the large quadrilateral clockwise as A (upper left), B (upper right), C (lower right), D (lower left). Thus the four regions are respectively APKW=8, PBSK=10, DWKT=18, and KSCT is what is sought. Reasoning: Let a=[ABK], b=[BCK], c=[CDK], d=[DAK]. Because the division points trisect the sides, AP=AW=1/3 of the corresponding whole side, PB=BS=2/3 of the corresponding whole side, DW=DT=2/3 of the corresponding whole side, and SC=CT=1/3 of the corresponding whole side. The small quadrilateral APKW can be divided along AK into two triangles, so APKW=(a+d)/3=8, giving a+d=24. The small quadrilateral PBSK can be divided along BK into two triangles, so PBSK=2(a+b)/3=10, giving a+b=15. The small quadrilateral DWKT can be divided along DK into two triangles, so DWKT=2(c+d)/3=18, giving c+d=27. The gray quadrilateral KSCT can be divided along CK into two triangles, so its area is (b+c)/3. Since b+c=(a+b)+(c+d)-(a+d)=15+27-24=18, therefore the gray area=(b+c)/3=18/3=6.

method.method_draft: Use an affine-coordinate setup. Label the outer quadrilateral A,B,C,D clockwise as in the image. From the trisection information and the visual placement, P=(1,0), W=(0,1), S=(1+2p/3,2q/3), and T=(2p/3,1+2q/3). Apply the shoelace formula to the four polygons seen in the image: area(APKW)=(u+v)/2=8, area(PBSK)=q+(pv-qu)/3=10, area(DWKT)=p+(qu-pv)/3=18. Adding the last two equations gives p+q=28, while the first gives u+v=16. The shaded polygon KSCT has shoelace area (p+q-u-v)/2, hence (28-16)/2=6.

The other labelled points divide the sides of the large quadrilateral into three equal parts. The numbers indicate the areas of the corresponding small quadrilaterals. What is the area of the shaded quadrilateral?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is a large quadrilateral. The interior point K is connected with several division points on the sides, dividing the large quadrilateral into 4 small quadrilaterals. The upper-left small quadrilateral is marked with area 8, the upper-right small quadrilateral is marked with area 10, the lower-left small quadrilateral is marked with area 18, and the lower-right gray small quadrilateral is marked with a question mark. The points P,Q; R,S; T,U; V,W on the sides respectively trisect the four sides of the large quadrilateral. According to the method, denote the four vertices of the large quadrilateral clockwise as A (upper left), B (upper right), C (lower right), D (lower left). Thus the four regions are respectively APKW=8, PBSK=10, DWKT=18, and KSCT is what is sought.
Reasoning: Let a=[ABK], b=[BCK], c=[CDK], d=[DAK]. Because the division points trisect the sides, AP=AW=1/3 of the corresponding whole side, PB=BS=2/3 of the corresponding whole side, DW=DT=2/3 of the corresponding whole side, and SC=CT=1/3 of the corresponding whole side. The small quadrilateral APKW can be divided along AK into two triangles, so APKW=(a+d)/3=8, giving a+d=24. The small quadrilateral PBSK can be divided along BK into two triangles, so PBSK=2(a+b)/3=10, giving a+b=15. The small quadrilateral DWKT can be divided along DK into two triangles, so DWKT=2(c+d)/3=18, giving c+d=27. The gray quadrilateral KSCT can be divided along CK into two triangles, so its area is (b+c)/3. Since b+c=(a+b)+(c+d)-(a+d)=15+27-24=18, therefore the gray area=(b+c)/3=18/3=6.
